title: Collections Policy for Missed Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans) Installments
content:
# Missed Installments and Removal from Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans)

## Policy

An installment on Budget Billing (Levelized and Equal Payment Plans) counts as missed when it is not paid in full by its due date. When the number of missed installments counted in the lookback reaches the plan's removal count, the member is removed from the plan and the deferred balance is settled on the next bill. An unpaid installment also bears the ordinary late charge where the plan applies it, and is subject to the ordinary disconnect rules where the plan applies them; the deferred balance itself is never past due until it is settled.

**The lookback** is the plan's lookback period of 12 calendar months ending on the current date. A missed installment is counted when the date on which its due date passed unpaid falls within that period.

**The removal count** is 2 missed installments on Levelized Billing Rolling Average, Budget Billing Annual Settle-Up, Budget Billing Quarterly Review, Farm Budget Billing and the Ten-Month Equal Payment Plan, and 1 on Small Business Budget Billing.

## Elements of the policy

| Element | Rule |
|---|---|
| What is a missed installment | An installment not paid in full by its due date; a partial payment leaves it missed |
| What is counted | Missed installments whose missed date falls within the 12 calendar months ending on the current date |
| When removal follows | When that count reaches the plan's removal count |
| What happens to the deferred balance | It is settled on the next bill |
| Late charge on an unpaid installment | The ordinary late charge, where the plan applies it (every plan does) |
| Disconnection | The unpaid installment is subject to the ordinary disconnect rules, where the plan applies them (every plan does) |
| Status of the deferred balance | Never past due until it is settled |

## Questions answered

**If a member pays part of an installment by the due date, is it missed?** Yes. An installment is missed when it is not paid in full by its due date.

**Does an installment missed long ago still count?** Only if the date on which it was missed falls within the 12 calendar months ending on the current date. *Hypothetical:* an installment missed 14 months ago is outside the lookback and is not counted; one missed 5 months ago is counted.

**Is the deferred balance treated as past due when an installment is missed?** No. The unpaid installment is what bears the late charge and is subject to disconnect rules; the deferred balance is never past due until it is settled.

## Hypothetical cases

- *Hypothetical:* a member on Farm Budget Billing has one installment missed 3 months ago and another missed this month. Both fall in the lookback, the count is 2, it reaches the removal count of 2, and the member is removed from the plan; the deferred balance is settled on the next bill.
- *Hypothetical:* a member on Budget Billing Annual Settle-Up has a single missed installment in the lookback. The count of 1 does not reach 2, so the removal rule is not met; the unpaid installment bears the ordinary late charge.
- *Hypothetical:* a member on Small Business Budget Billing misses one installment. The count of 1 reaches the removal count of 1, and the member is removed from the plan.
